newsitem.title: USA: Cook County board adopts bad debt write off policy.
newsitem.headline: Cook County board adopts bad debt write off policy.

text.p: Cook County Board approved a basic policy Thursday for writing off bad debts accumulated at its public health facilities, the chief financial officer for the bureau of health services said.
The bureau seeks to write off an estimated $1.036 billion of bad debts rung up by patients at its public hospital in Chicago from 1975 to 1992, Chief Financial Officer Alvin Holley said.
The policy, which is still subject to approval from the Cook County state's attorney's office, will allow the bureau to clear the books "when all collection efforts are exhausted," Holley said.
According to a Chicago Tribune article published in May, patients have amassed another $270 million of debts for services rendered since 1992 that have not yet been declared uncollectable.

An outside auditor told the Tribune the write-off would have no impact on Cook County or its bond rating. It also would have no impact on health facilities operations or the construction of a new hospital.
The Los Angeles County health system has much larger uncollectable debts and the $1 billion of unpaid bills was not considered extraordinary, the Tribune reported.
